value.account:
CHANGED
- State: RunState.result_persistence_profile (optional, omitted from to_dict when absent, validated in __post_init__ so construction, initialize and load all fail closed with a ValueError naming the profile). StateManager.initialize takes result_persistence_profile and writes it with the first state write. Four atomic StateManager methods (begin_eligible_pure_visit, reuse_interrupted_eligible_pure_visit, settle_eligible_pure_success/failure) and matching _CallFrameStateManager methods; both share helpers in pure_replay_progress.py.
- Selection: orchestrator run (frontend_build present), resume --force-restart (.orc candidate) and fresh non-iterative child frames (callee provenance.frontend_kind == workflow_lisp, runtime_step_id is None, no existing frame; a fresh retry has no existing frame so it selects too). _CallFrameStateManager validates a malformed existing frame (message contains 'existing call-frame state') before any mkdir/write; load_existing_call_frame_read_only added. Force-restart no longer writes the merged observability into the source run (it only feeds the new root), so the source stays byte-identical.
- New modules (each under 500 lines, re-exported from orchestrator/workflow/pure_result_replay.py): pure_replay_index.py (eligibility, SCC-based multiple-visit detection, typed ref resolution, type-directed literal validation incl. inactive union members, topological order, PureResultReplayIndexError), pure_replay_progress.py (witness, exact shell build/validate, classify), pure_replay_runtime.py (PureReplayRuntime: caches, revalidated overlay, replay_node, address resolution, boundary requirements/leaf audit, persisted-surface conflict audit), pure_replay_coordinator.py (executor wiring).
- Executor: eligible pure nodes begin/reuse their visit via the state manager instead of _increment_step_visit+start_step, execute without any result bundle (execute_pure_projection(bundle_backed=False)), and settle through OutcomeRecorder.persist_step_result(eligible_pure_settlement=witness) (shell to disk and summary emitter, full result kept in memory). Failure/skip paths get the settlement automatically in _persist_step_result. Resume: surface and progress audits run before the prologue; the restart node is determined once in execute() and passed down (ResumePlanner.determine_default_resume_decision gained a restart_node_id keyword); leaf audit + replay run before the loop; reconstructed rows are installed into the in-memory state only after the default-resume decision. Failures end the run with error.type pure_result_replay_unavailable and error.context.reason. Provider observation manager is now created at the start of execute() and closed once.
- Checkpoints: emit_runtime_shadow_record skips eligible pure points; capture_restore_payload omits bindings sourced from eligible pure steps; default resume filters eligible points out of _nearest_prior_effect_boundary and admits VALIDATED_FRAME_ENTRY_REPLAY (validated_frame_entry_replay, checkpoint_id null) as the only zero-record case, else FAIL_CLOSED with lexical_default_resume_prior_boundary_not_restorable.
- specs/state.md documents the profile. tests/test_pure_result_replay_profile.py (36 behavioural tests incl. end-to-end run/resume with fake effects counting dispatches, CLI run + force-restart). Two existing provider-observation tests were updated because they asserted construction-time manager creation, which the requirement reverses.

VERIFICATION
Full suite (excluding tests/e2e): 140 failures, all in the pre-existing baseline set (I re-ran the failing files with my changes stashed: same provider-isolation/materialization/tmux/socket failures; two extra failures under load passed in isolation). The 6 regressions I introduced along the way were fixed (observation tests updated, executor wrapper tolerant of stubbed default-resume signature, class-level _pure_replay default).

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED
- Computing the restart node before the prologue for everything: rejected, provider-recovery in the prologue can change it; only surface/progress audits run pre-prologue.
- Installing replayed rows into state before the default-resume decision: tried first, it made progress classification see non-shell rows and fail closed; moved installation after the decision.
- Making publishing pure nodes eligible: rejected, they own lineage; they are ineligible (publishes_artifacts).
- Passing restart_node_id to the executor's default-resume wrapper unconditionally: broke existing stubs, so it is passed only if the wrapper accepts it.

NOT COVERED / GUESSES (please check against your acceptance tests)
- Interface guesses: evaluate_node(node, overlay_state) receives a str-subclass node handle (equals the node id and exposes node attributes) and returns a step-result-like dict; resolve_bundle_path is called with the node id; load_existing_call_frame_read_only returns a RunState; scope mismatch sets expected_scope to the requested scope_kind and actual_scope to the bundle's scope; runtime always indexes under scope 'root'.
- 'Durable owner' for frame-entry replay is interpreted as: validation of profile, progress witnesses and bound-input leaves must pass, else fail closed; I did not add a separate durable-owner test.
- Resume of an imported child frame with eligible pure nodes was not exercised end to end (only selection of the profile in the child frame); union-row exactness is covered at unit level only; reachability_ambiguous is only reachable through the index API; no test for unrelated restore-payload omission beyond the policy fixture run.
- Pure nodes referencing other nodes' text-substituted fields (e.g. ${steps...} in command strings) are only found for boundary requirements by substring match on presentation keys.
